memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: However, when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, they resorted to a ruse: They went as a delegation whose donkeys were loaded with worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended. They put worn and patched sandals on their feet and wore old clothes. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy. — Josh 9:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Gibeonites take a different path from the other kings. Instead of fighting, they scheme. Knowing that Israel was commanded not to make treaties with the nations of the land, they disguise themselves as travellers from a distant country. Every detail is carefully staged: worn-out sacks, cracked wineskins, patched sandals, mouldy bread. It is an elaborate, convincing deception.

We should notice something honestly here. The Gibeonites were driven by fear, and their fear was mixed with a kind of faith — they had concluded that Israel's God was real and unstoppable, and they wanted to survive. Yet the way they pursued survival was through lies and trickery rather than honest appeal. Their instinct to seek peace with God's people was not entirely wrong; their method was.

There is a lesson here about how we pursue even good desires. It is possible to want the right thing and go about it in the wrong way. The Gibeonites wanted to live, and they were right that safety lay with Israel's God. But they sought it through deception instead of coming openly and honestly.

How much better simply to come to God in truth. We never need to manipulate or scheme our way toward Him. Unlike the Gibeonites, who felt they had to trick their way into safety, we are invited to come "with sincere hearts" and full assurance (Heb 10:22). God welcomes honest seekers. The way to God through Christ is not through cleverness or pretence, but through simple, truthful faith. We come as we are, and He receives us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever pursued a good desire through wrong or dishonest means?
2. Why is it tempting to scheme rather than come to God honestly?
3. How does it free you to know God welcomes honest, sincere seekers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from pursuing even good things through wrong means. Teach me to come to You honestly, with a sincere heart, trusting that You welcome me as I am. Amen.
